reasoning.text: July 2026 real average hourly earnings forecast

The resolver is BLS Real Earnings Table A-1: the seasonally adjusted over-the-month percent change in real average hourly earnings for all employees on private nonfarm payrolls. This is the all-employees, CPI-U-deflated variant, not the production-and-nonsupervisory CPI-W series; resolve only to the July first print, rounded to BLS's one decimal, with no later revision substitution.

reasoning.result: The official BLS calendar lists Real Earnings for July 2026 at 08:30 AM on August 12, 2026; it also lists the July CPI release at 08:30 AM on August 12, 2026.

reasoning.call: Fetched the latest BLS Real Earnings Table A-1 and May 2026 Real Earnings release.
reasoning.result: Table A-1 reports real average hourly earnings month-over-month changes of -0.6 percent in March 2026, -0.5 percent in April, and -0.1 percent in May; May nominal average hourly earnings rose 0.3 percent while CPI-U rose 0.5 percent.

reasoning.call: Fetched the BLS March and April 2026 archived Real Earnings releases for same-variant history.
reasoning.result: The March release reported January 2026 real average hourly earnings at 0.3 percent, February at 0.1 percent, and March at -0.6 percent month over month; the April release reported April at -0.5 percent. These are the same Table A-1 all-employees, seasonally adjusted CPI-U-deflated variant.

reasoning.call: Fetched the BLS June 2026 Employment Situation release for the latest nominal-pay signal.
reasoning.result: BLS reported that June average hourly earnings for all employees on private nonfarm payrolls rose 13 cents, or 0.3 percent, to $37.64; the total-private series was $37.51 in May and $37.64 in June.

reasoning.text: The five-observation reference class has a base rate of -0.16 percent per month: January through May were 0.3, 0.1, -0.6, -0.5, and -0.1 percent. The latest two releases show real pay falling as CPI-U outran modest nominal wage gains, so the baseline remains slightly negative.

Prior/update/interval: Persistence prior is the January-May 2026 first-print Table A-1 change sample [0.3, 0.1, -0.6, -0.5, -0.1], with mean = -0.16 and sample sigma = 0.38 percentage points. The adjustment components are a +0.1 point pull from June's 0.3 percent nominal-pay growth, offset by continued CPI-U deflator uncertainty and no assumed July CPI slowdown, yielding -0.1 percent. The 80% half-width is 1.28*0.38 = 0.49 percentage points; rounded to the release's one-decimal precision, implied bounds are -0.6 to 0.4 percent.

upside risk: a July CPI-U print near zero alongside another roughly 0.3 percent nominal hourly-pay gain would lift real earnings above 0.4 percent. downside risk: a CPI-U increase materially above nominal wage growth, or a weak/negative nominal-pay print, would land below -0.6 percent. A sharp energy-driven CPI move or unusual seasonal-factor outcome is the main outside the interval scenario.
